event.title: Ghostly Bangor Walking Tour
event.description: The Bangor Historical Society’s Ghostly Bangor Walking Tour features tales of unsolved mysteries, murder, and energies that may still linger in the Queen City. Tours stroll through the streets of Downtown Bangor and last around 90 minutes. Tickets are $12. Advanced ticketing is required. Our tours are capped at 25 guests, and tickets sell out quickly. Tickets must be purchased by noon of the date of the tour. To purchase tickets or for more info please visit our website or e-mail us at curator@bangorhistoricalsociety.org. Tours depart from the Bangor Historical Society’s Thomas A. Hill House (159 Union Street, Bangor) at 7 p.m. Parking is available on High Street. A note on inclement weather: tours will be cancelled if there is a chance of thunderstorms but not if only rain is in the forecast.

event.title: Darker Mount Hope Cemetery Tour October 23rd
event.description: Explore Bangor’s dark side and take a walk amid the shadows during the Bangor Historical Society’s Darker Mount Hope Cemetery Tour, Friday and Saturday, October 23 & 24, 2026. As the night deepens while you meander the paved paths, a cast of living souls will regale you with dramatic, moving, touching, mysterious, and even spooky stories —sprinkled with a bit of history, of course— about the permanent residents of Mount Hope. This nighttime walking tour of one of the oldest garden cemeteries in the country is a seasonal favorite. Tours are conducted on foot and are no more than one mile, but may include stairs, hills, and uneven terrain. We recommend sturdy footwear, warm clothing, and a flashlight. Tours are conducted rain or shine. Advanced Tickets are required and are sold for specific start times, starting at 6 pm. Tickets will go on sale to the public on Thursday, September 24th, at noon. Guests should enter Mount Hope Cemetery at 1048 State Street, Bangor, and check in near the Superintendent’s Lodge at no sooner than 20 minutes before their departure time. Parking is available along both sides of the cemetery entry road, accessible via the State Street gate. Use “Second Maine Regiment Memorial” into GPS for the correct entrance gate location. Direct questions to the museum curator via email at curator@bangorhistoricalsociety.org or by calling 207-942-1900.

event.title: History in Focus:  The Brady Gang Shootout
event.description: Join us for a one-time only event on Saturday, October 24th at 10am. The morning will begin with a meeting inside the Thomas A. Hill House, where we will examine photos and artifacts related to the FBI’s most wanted gangster in 1937. We will follow Al Brady and his gang and learn of the crimes that led to their eventual demise on Central Street on that bright October morning in 1937. Following the talk, we will walk to the site of the shooting to see where history happened 89 years ago. We have a limited number of tickets available for this special event at $20 per ticket.
